ai.description: *Kurixalus yangi* is a small treefrog (25–30 mm) with a brownish body, dark X-shaped dorsal markings, and granular skin. It features distinct dermal fringes on the limbs and reddish-brown iris coloration.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Kurixalus yangi* is best distinguished from similar species by the presence of distinct, fleshy dermal fringes along the outer edges of its forearms and tarsi.
ai.habitat: *Kurixalus yangi* inhabits subtropical evergreen forests and bamboo thickets in Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Yang's Frill-limbed Treefrog is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by blending into its surroundings with excellent camouflage against tree bark.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Kurixalus yangi* is an egg-laying species that breeds during the monsoon season, depositing clutches of approximately 30–50 eggs in foam nests over water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Kurixalus yangi* is found in Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, inhabiting tropical forests at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Kurixalus yangi* consists of a series of rapid, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard from vegetation near forest pools or streams.
